lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: That codding spirit had they from their mother,

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: As sure a card as ever won the set;

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: That bloody mind, I think, they learn'd of me,

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: As true a dog as ever fought at head.

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: Well, let my deeds be witness of my worth.

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: I train'd thy brethren to that guileful hole

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: Where the dead corpse of Bassianus lay:

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: I wrote the letter that thy father found,

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: And hid the gold within that letter mention'd,

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: Confederate with the queen and her two sons:

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: And what not done, that thou hast cause to rue,

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: Wherein I had no stroke of mischief in't?

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: I play'd the cheater for thy father's hand;

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: And, when I had it, drew myself apart,

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: And almost broke my heart with extreme laughter:

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: I pry'd me through the crevice of a wall

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: When, for his hand, he had his two sons' heads;

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: Beheld his tears, and laugh'd so heartily

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: That both mine eyes were rainy like to his:

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: And when I told the empress of this sport,

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: She swooned almost at my pleasing tale,

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: And for my tidings gave me twenty kisses.

lines.speaker: A Goth
lines.text: What, canst thou say all this and never blush?

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: Ay, like a black dog, as the saying is.

lines.speaker: Lucius
lines.text: Art thou not sorry for these heinous deeds?

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: Ay, that I had not done a thousand more.

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: Even now I curse the day,--and yet, I think,

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: Few come within the compass of my curse,--

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: Wherein I did not some notorious ill:

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: As, kill a man, or else devise his death;

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: Ravish a maid, or plot the way to do it;

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: Accuse some innocent, and forswear myself;

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: Set deadly enmity between two friends;

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: Make poor men's cattle stray and break their necks;

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: Set fire on barns and hay-stacks in the night,

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: And bid the owners quench them with their tears.

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: Oft have I digg'd up dead men from their graves,

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: And set them upright at their dear friends' doors,

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: Even when their sorrows almost were forgot;

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: And on their skins, as on the bark of trees,

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: Have with my knife carved in Roman letters,

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: 'Let not your sorrow die, though I am dead.'

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: Tut, I have done a thousand dreadful things

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: As willingly as one would kill a fly;

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: And nothing grieves me heartily indeed

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: But that I cannot do ten thousand more.

lines.speaker: Lucius
lines.text: Bring down the devil; for he must not die

lines.speaker: Lucius
lines.text: So sweet a death as hanging presently.

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: If there be devils, would I were a devil,

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: To live and burn in everlasting fire,

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: So I might have your company in hell

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: But to torment you with my bitter tongue!

lines.speaker: Lucius
lines.text: Sirs, stop his mouth, and let him speak no more.

lines.speaker: Third Goth
lines.text: My lord, there is a messenger from Rome

lines.speaker: Third Goth
lines.text: Desires to be admitted to your presence.

lines.speaker: Lucius
lines.text: Let him come near.

lines.speaker: Lucius
lines.text: Welcome, Aemilius. What's the news from Rome?

lines.speaker: Aemilius
lines.text: Lord Lucius, and you princes of the Goths,

lines.speaker: Aemilius
lines.text: The Roman emperor greets you all by me;

lines.speaker: Aemilius
lines.text: And, for he understands you are in arms,

lines.speaker: Aemilius
lines.text: He craves a parley at your father's house,

lines.speaker: Aemilius
lines.text: Willing you to demand your hostages,

lines.speaker: Aemilius
lines.text: And they shall be immediately deliver'd.

lines.speaker: First Goth
lines.text: What says our general?

lines.speaker: Lucius
lines.text: Aemilius, let the emperor give his pledges

lines.speaker: Lucius
lines.text: Unto my father and my uncle Marcus.

lines.speaker: Lucius
lines.text: And we will come.--March away.

stage_directions: Enter TAMORA, DEMETRIUS and CHIRON, disguised.

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: Thus, in this strange and sad habiliment,

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: I will encounter with Andronicus,

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: And say I am Revenge, sent from below

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: To join with him and right his heinous wrongs.

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: Knock at his study, where they say he keeps

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: To ruminate strange plots of dire revenge;

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: Tell him Revenge is come to join with him,

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: And work confusion on his enemies.

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Who doth molest my contemplation?

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Is it your trick to make me ope the door,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: That so my sad decrees may fly away

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: And all my study be to no effect?

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: You are deceiv'd: for what I mean to do

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: See here in bloody lines I have set down;

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: And what is written shall be executed.

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: Titus, I am come to talk with thee.

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: No, not a word: how can I grace my talk,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Wanting a hand to give it action?

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Thou hast the odds of me; therefore no more.

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: If thou didst know me, thou wouldst talk with me.

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: I am not mad; I know thee well enough:

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Witness this wretched stump, witness these crimson lines;

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Witness these trenches made by grief and care;

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Witness the tiring day and heavy night;

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Witness all sorrow, that I know thee well

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: For our proud empress, mighty Tamora:

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Is not thy coming for my other hand?

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: Know thou, sad man, I am not Tamora;

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: She is thy enemy and I thy friend:

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: I am Revenge; sent from the infernal kingdom

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: To ease the gnawing vulture of thy mind

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: By working wreakful vengeance on thy foes.

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: Come down and welcome me to this world's light;

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: Confer with me of murder and of death:

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: There's not a hollow cave or lurking-place,

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: No vast obscurity or misty vale,

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: Where bloody murder or detested rape

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: Can couch for fear but I will find them out;

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: And in their ears tell them my dreadful name,--

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: Revenge, which makes the foul offender quake.

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Art thou Revenge? and art thou sent to me

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: To be a torment to mine enemies?

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: I am; therefore come down and welcome me.

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Do me some service ere I come to thee.

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Lo, by thy side where Rape and Murder stands;

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Now give some surance that thou art Revenge,--

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Stab them, or tear them on thy chariot wheels;

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: And then I'll come and be thy waggoner,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: And whirl along with thee about the globe.

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Provide thee two proper palfreys, black as jet,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: To hale thy vengeful waggon swift away,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: And find out murderers in their guilty caves:

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: And when thy car is loaden with their heads

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: I will dismount, and by the waggon-wheel

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Trot, like a servile footman, all day long,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Even from Hyperion's rising in the east

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Until his very downfall in the sea:

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: And day by day I'll do this heavy task,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: So thou destroy Rapine and Murder there.

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: These are my ministers, and come with me.

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Are they thy ministers? what are they call'd?

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: Rapine and Murder; therefore called so

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: 'Cause they take vengeance of such kind of men.

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Good Lord, how like the empress' sons they are!

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: And you the empress! But we worldly men

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Have miserable, mad, mistaking eyes.

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: O sweet Revenge, now do I come to thee;

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: And, if one arm's embracement will content thee,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: I will embrace thee in it by and by.

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: This closing with him fits his lunacy:

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: Whate'er I forge to feed his brain-sick fiits,

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: Do you uphold and maintain in your speeches,

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: For now he firmly takes me for Revenge;

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: And, being credulous in this mad thought,

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: I'll make him send for Lucius his son;

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: And whilst I at a banquet hold him sure,

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: I'll find some cunning practice out of hand

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: To scatter and disperse the giddy Goths,

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: Or, at the least, make them his enemies.

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: See, here he comes, and I must ply my theme.

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Long have I been forlorn, and all for thee:

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Welcome, dread fury, to my woeful house;--

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Rapine and Murder, you are welcome too:--

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: How like the empress and her sons you are!

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Well are you fitted, had you but a Moor:

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Could not all hell afford you such a devil?--

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: For well I wot the empress never wags

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: But in her company there is a Moor;

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: And, would you represent our queen aright,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: It were convenient you had such a devil:

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: But welcome as you are. What shall we do?

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: What wouldst thou have us do, Andronicus?

lines.speaker: Demetrius
lines.text: Show me a murderer, I'll deal with him.

lines.speaker: Chiron
lines.text: Show me a villain that hath done a rape,

lines.speaker: Chiron
lines.text: And I am sent to be reveng'd on him.

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: Show me a thousand that hath done thee wrong,

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: And I will be revenged on them all.

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Look round about the wicked streets of Rome,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: And when thou find'st a man that's like thyself,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Good Murder, stab him; he's a murderer.--

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Go thou with him; and when it is thy hap

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: To find another that is like to thee,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Good Rapine, stab him; he is a ravisher.--

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Go thou with them; and in the emperor's court

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: There is a queen, attended by a Moor;

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Well mayst thou know her by thine own proportion,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: For up and down she doth resemble thee;

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: I pray thee, do on them some violent death;

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: They have been violent to me and mine.

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: Well hast thou lesson'd us; this shall we do.

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: But would it please thee, good Andronicus,

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: To send for Lucius, thy thrice-valiant son,

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: Who leads towards Rome a band of warlike Goths,

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: And bid him come and banquet at thy house;

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: When he is here, even at thy solemn feast,

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: I will bring in the empress and her sons,

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: The emperor himself, and all thy foes;

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: And at thy mercy shall they stoop and kneel,

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: And on them shalt thou ease thy angry heart.

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: What says Andronicus to this device?

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Marcus, my brother!--'tis sad Titus calls.

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Go, gentle Marcus, to thy nephew Lucius;

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Thou shalt inquire him out among the Goths:

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Bid him repair to me, and bring with him

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Some of the chiefest princes of the Goths;

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Bid him encamp his soldiers where they are:

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Tell him the emperor and the empress too

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Feast at my house, and he shall feast with them.

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: This do thou for my love; and so let him,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: As he regards his aged father's life.

lines.speaker: Marcus Andronicus
lines.text: This will I do, and soon return again.

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: Now will I hence about thy business,

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: And take my ministers along with me.

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Nay, nay, let Rape and Murder stay with me,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Or else I'll call my brother back again,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: And cleave to no revenge but Lucius.

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: What say you, boys? will you abide with him,

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: Whiles I go tell my lord the emperor

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: How I have govern'd our determin'd jest?

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: Yield to his humour, smooth and speak him fair,

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: And tarry with him till I come again.

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: I knew them all, though they suppose me mad,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: And will o'er reach them in their own devices,--

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: A pair of cursed hell-hounds and their dam.

lines.speaker: Demetrius
lines.text: Madam, depart at pleasure; leave us here.

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: Farewell, Andronicus: Revenge now goes

lines.speaker: Tamora
lines.text: To lay a complot to betray thy foes.

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: I know thou dost; and, sweet Revenge, farewell!

lines.speaker: Chiron
lines.text: Tell us, old man, how shall we be employ'd?

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Tut, I have work enough for you to do.--

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Publius, come hither, Caius, and Valentine.

lines.speaker: Publius
lines.text: What is your will?

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Know you these two?

lines.speaker: Publius
lines.text: The empress' sons, I take them: Chiron, Demetrius.

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Fie, Publius, fie! thou art too much deceiv'd,--

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: The one is Murder, Rape is the other's name;

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: And therefore bind them, gentle Publius:--

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Caius and Valentine, lay hands on them:--

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Oft have you heard me wish for such an hour,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: And now I find it; therefore bind them sure;

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: And stop their mouths if they begin to cry.

stage_directions: Exit. PUBLIUS &c., lay hands on CHIRON and DEMETRIUS.

lines.speaker: Chiron
lines.text: Villains, forbear! we are the empress' sons.

lines.speaker: Publius
lines.text: And therefore do we what we are commanded.--

lines.speaker: Publius
lines.text: Stop close their mouths, let them not speak a word.

lines.speaker: Publius
lines.text: Is he sure bound? look that you bind them fast.

stage_directions: Re-enter TITUS ANDRONICUS, with LAVINIA; he bearing a knife and she a basin.

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Come, come, Lavinia; look, thy foes are bound.--

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Sirs, stop their mouths, let them not speak to me;

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: But let them hear what fearful words I utter.--

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: O villains, Chiron and Demetrius!

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Here stands the spring whom you have stain'd with mud;

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: This goodly summer with your winter mix'd.

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: You kill'd her husband; and for that vile fault

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Two of her brothers were condemn'd to death,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: My hand cut off and made a merry jest;

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Both her sweet hands, her tongue, and that, more dear

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Than hands or tongue, her spotless chastity,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Inhuman traitors, you constrain'd and forc'd.

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: What would you say, if I should let you speak?

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Villains, for shame you could not beg for grace.

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Hark, wretches! how I mean to martyr you.

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: This one hand yet is left to cut your throats,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Whiles that Lavinia 'tween her stumps doth hold

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: The basin that receives your guilty blood.

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: You know your mother means to feast with me,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: And calls herself Revenge, and thinks me mad:--

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Hark, villains! I will grind your bones to dust,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: And with your blood and it I'll make a paste;

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: And of the paste a coffin I will rear,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: And make two pasties of your shameful heads;

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: And bid that strumpet, your unhallow'd dam,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Like to the earth, swallow her own increase.

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: This is the feast that I have bid her to,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: And this the banquet she shall surfeit on;

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: For worse than Philomel you us'd my daughter,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: And worse than Progne I will be reveng'd:

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: And now prepare your throats. Lavinia, come

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Receive the blood: and when that they are dead,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Let me go grind their bones to powder small,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: And with this hateful liquor temper it;

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: And in that paste let their vile heads be bak'd.

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: Come, come, be every one officious

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: To make this banquet; which I wish may prove

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: More stern and bloody than the Centaurs' feast.

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: So, now bring them in, for I will play the cook,

lines.speaker: Titus Andronicus
lines.text: And see them ready against their mother comes.

scenes.setting: Rome. A Pavilion in TITUS'S Gardens, with tables, &c.

stage_directions: Enter LUCIUS, MARCUS, and GOTHS, with AARON prisoner.

lines.speaker: Lucius
lines.text: Uncle Marcus, since 'tis my father's mind

lines.speaker: Lucius
lines.text: That I repair to Rome, I am content.

lines.speaker: First Goth
lines.text: And ours with thine, befall what fortune will.

lines.speaker: Lucius
lines.text: Good uncle, take you in this barbarous Moor,

lines.speaker: Lucius
lines.text: This ravenous tiger, this accursed devil;

lines.speaker: Lucius
lines.text: Let him receive no sustenance, fetter him,

lines.speaker: Lucius
lines.text: Till he be brought unto the empress' face

lines.speaker: Lucius
lines.text: For testimony of her foul proceedings:

lines.speaker: Lucius
lines.text: And see the ambush of our friends be strong;

lines.speaker: Lucius
lines.text: I fear the emperor means no good to us.

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: Some devil whisper curses in my ear,

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: And prompt me that my tongue may utter forth

lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.text: The venomous malice of my swelling heart!

lines.speaker: Lucius
lines.text: Away, inhuman dog, unhallowed slave!--

lines.speaker: Lucius
lines.text: Sirs, help our uncle to convey him in.--

stage_directions: Exeunt GOTHS with AARON. Flourish within. The trumpets show the emperor is at hand.

lines.text: What, hath the firmament more suns than one?

lines.speaker: Lucius
lines.text: What boots it thee to call thyself the sun?

lines.speaker: Marcus Andronicus
lines.text: Rome's emperor, and nephew, break the parle;

lines.speaker: Marcus Andronicus
lines.text: These quarrels must be quietly debated.

lines.speaker: Marcus Andronicus
lines.text: The feast is ready, which the careful Titus
